title: The Loom of Mist
story: High on the cliff-stairs, Wexlowry the Fogshear weaves a wall of mist across the only path home, and three shepherd children are trapped on the far side. Mr 6 counts the mist wall: it is 96 feet thick, and Wexlowry weaves 6 more feet onto it every minute. But Mr 6's sword of sunlight burns away 14 feet of mist each minute.
question: How many minutes until Mr 6 burns completely through the mist wall?
solution: Each minute the wall really shrinks by 14 - 6 = 8 feet.
praise: Dividing was exactly the right instinct — the missing step was subtracting the mist Wexlowry weaves back each minute.
hint: The wall loses 14 feet but gains 6 every minute — find the NET change for one minute first.
victory: The last shreds of fog curled up like startled cats and blew away, and Wexlowry huffed off to weave scarves instead. The shepherd children walked home on a staircase full of sunlight.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight with a blue cape holding a glowing sunlight sword against a towering wall of swirling grey mist on a cliff staircase, a tattered fog-weaving spirit hovering above, pale dawn light breaking through.
